title: EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Annex III: AI-Enabled Products — December 2026 Enforcement Guide | Council of AI
context: 2026-08-30 engine cycle — The EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation 2024/2847) enters mandatory enforcement for Annex III products with digital elements on 11 December 2026. AI-enabled products that process data, make automated decisions, or integrate machine-learning components fall within scope. This seed page provides answer-first guidance on how the Council of AI verified measurement credential maps to CRA essential cybersecurity requirements, vulnerability disclosure obligations, and conformity assessment procedures for Class I and Class II AI-enabled products.
body: The EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) mandates that all products with digital elements placed on the EU market meet essential cybersecurity requirements across their entire lifecycle. For AI-enabled products, this intersects with the EU AI Act in specific and actionable ways. Three pillars matter. (1) Essential cybersecurity requirements (Annex I): AI systems must be designed to limit attack surfaces, protect against unauthorised access, and ensure data minimisation. For machine-learning pipelines, this means model weights must be integrity-verified at load time, inference APIs must resist prompt injection and adversarial inputs, and training-data provenance must be auditable. The Council of AI verified measurement credential can embed a CRA-compliance assertion — linking a product's SBOM (software bill of materials), vulnerability disclosure report, and conformity assessment record into a single signed, independently verifiable measurement stream. (2) Vulnerability disclosure (Article 13): manufacturers must establish a coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) process and report actively exploited vulnerabilities to ENISA within 24 hours of awareness. The Council of AI containment index extends this: each incident is a signed event in a real-time containment ledger, giving manufacturers an independently verifiable disclosure timeline that satisfies Article 13(3) record-keeping. (3) Conformity assessment for Annex III products: Class I AI products (lower risk) can self-assess under Module A; Class II AI products (higher risk, including safety-critical AI systems) require third-party assessment under Module B+C or Module H. The Council Signal measurement framework provides the evidentiary substrate for both — a signed, timestamped, cross-referenced bundle that a notified body can validate in minutes rather than weeks. The enforcement clock is running: manufacturers selling AI-enabled products into the EU must have their CRA conformity assessment completed by 11 December 2026. The grace period for existing products ends June 2027. The Council of AI compliance mapping covers CRA ↔ EU AI Act ↔ NIS2 in a single crosswalk, eliminating duplicate assessment effort. No sovereign-labelling shortcut exists — only verified measurement rooted in cryptographic signing of each assessment step, from SBOM generation through vulnerability disclosure to post-market surveillance.
